item.title: Recalling the heroism of FDNY firefighters at ground zero on 9/11 | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Hundreds of firefighters died during 9/11 rescue efforts at the World Trade Center. FDNY members who were there say 9/11 and its aftermath are a part of who they are.

item.title: Kennedy Center foyer ceiling partially falls amid Trump's push for renovations
item.description: No one was injured when a piece of the ceiling inside the Kennedy Center's grand foyer partially collapsed Friday evening, said Roma Daravi, the center's vice president for public relations.

item.title: U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for Iran targeting warships
item.description: Iran fired ballistic missiles at a U.S. aircraft carrier and a destroyer, but the ships were able to evade the attacks, Central Command said.

item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Sept. 6)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Trump delivers $10 million to Ken Paxton in first major contribution of midterms
item.description: President Trump's MAGA Inc. super PAC had previously only given one donation this midterm cycle: about $800,000 to Darline Graham.

item.title: Witkoff, Kushner visit Moscow in latest push to end war in Ukraine
item.description: Presidents Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy agreed to pause strikes on each other's capitals while U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner hold talks to revive peace efforts.

item.title: Guyana latest "third country" to accept migrants deported from U.S.
item.description: Guyana is one of more than 30 nations that have now signed deals with the Trump administration as part of President Trump's crackdown on illegal immigration.

item.title: U.S. ambassador calls ongoing West Bank settler violence an "act of terror"
item.description: U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee met with about 10 Palestinian American residents who described the impact of the violence on their lives and properties.

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Improvement Movement performs "On the Bus"
item.description: Improvement Movement is one of Atlanta's most exciting new bands. They say their third album, "Your Perfect Real Life," is sure to "inundate your ears" with as much good as you can reasonably feel these days. Here's Improvement Movement with "On the Bus."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Improvement Movement performs "In the Morning"
item.description: Improvement Movement is one of Atlanta's most exciting new bands. They say their third album, "Your Perfect Real Life," is sure to "inundate your ears" with as much good as you can reasonably feel these days. Here's Improvement Movement with "In the Morning."

item.title: Saturday Sessions: Improvement Movement performs "I Do"
item.description: Improvement Movement is one of Atlanta's most exciting new bands. They say their third album, "Your Perfect Real Life," is sure to "inundate your ears" with as much good as you can reasonably feel these days. Here's Improvement Movement with "I Do."

item.title: Colombia drone attack by suspected guerrillas kills 3 soldiers, army says
item.description: Recently elected President Abelardo de la Espriella​ condemned the attack.

item.title: "Star Trek" celebrates 60 years
item.description: "Star Trek" debuted 60 years ago, and while it only lasted three seasons, it birthed decades of spinoff shows and movies and a dedicated fanbase like no other.

item.title: Documentary looks at first all-female crew to compete in America's Cup
item.description: A new documentary looks at the Mighty Mary, the first sailboat to compete with an all-female crew in the prestigious sailing competition, the America's Cup.

item.title: The man determining the monetary value of lives lost on 9/11 | 60 Minutes Archive
item.description: Kenneth Feinberg, an arbitration lawyer, was tasked by Congress with determining the compensation due to families who lost someone as a result of the 9/11 terror attacks.

item.title: Salt Hank's French dip sandwich takes over the U.S. Open
item.description: Henry Laporte brought his viral $38 French dip sandwich to the U.S. Open for the first time. Laporte is winning fans despite having no formal training as a chef.

item.title: Checking in with Stuyvesant High School students 25 years after 9/11
item.description: The students of Stuyvesant High School were just three blocks from the World Trade Center on Sept. 11, 2001. Lila Nordstrom, a student at the school at the time and author of "Some Kids Left Behind," became an advocate for those sickened by the toxic dust.

item.title: Looking back at the Jerry Lewis Muscular Dystrophy Telethon after 60 years
item.description: The first 24-hour Jerry Lewis Muscular Dystrophy Association telethon aired 60 years ago on Saturday. The staple of Labor Day weekend featured established stars like Dolly Parton and young comics like Jimmy Fallon.

item.title: Races to keep an eye with midterm elections just 2 months away
item.description: From the Michigan Senate race between Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers to the Texas Senate competition between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton, there are many hotly contested midterm election races.

item.title: What comes next after mistrial in Lindsay Clancy murder trial?
item.description: The mistrial declared in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy leaves many questions about whether there will be another trial and about our understanding of postpartum psychosis.

item.title: Hiring stronger than expected in August
item.description: President Trump took a victory lap as the United States added nearly three times as many jobs as analysts expected for August, while unemployment held steady at 4.1%.

item.title: 2 more rescued from debris in Nepal 10 days after devastating floods
item.description: The rescue brings the total to three workers saved from a hydropower tunnel, after two other workers were freed a day before.

item.title: Painting looted by Nazis to be returned to collector's heir
item.description: The painting was among the artworks looted and sold under duress to Nazi officials from art dealer Jacques Goudstikker after Adolf Hitler's Germany invaded the Netherlands in 1940.

item.title: Top military officials faced polygraphs over leaks on munitions, sources say
item.description: Some of the highest-ranking officials in the U.S. military were subjected to polygraph tests as part of a sweeping leak probe, U.S. officials briefed on the matter told CBS News.

item.title: 9/5: CBS Saturday Morning
item.description: Judge declares mistrial in Lindsay Clancy murder trial, job hiring numbers are better than expected and an airline passenger is duct taped to a chair after an outburst.

item.title: American Airlines passenger duct-taped to seat after mid-flight outburst
item.description: A picture shows the man with multiple loops of tape around his wrists, torso and head.

item.title: BOP faces scrutiny over exclusive deal to sell nicotine pouches to prisoners
item.description: The BOP in July entered into an exclusive arrangement with a Florida startup that allows the company to sell federal prisoners nicotine pouches that are not authorized by the FDA.

item.title: Supreme Court sides with Republicans in fight over broadcast ad rates
item.description: The Supreme Court left in place guidance from the Federal Communications Commission that allows political parties and committees access to cheaper rates for political ads.

item.title: Judge extends block on Postal Service's new Trump-backed mail-in ballot requirements
item.description: A federal judge extended her block on the U.S. Postal Service's new requirements for mail voting, as states prepare to begin sending mail ballots to voters for the November midterm elections.

item.title: How AI is reshaping the U.S. Open for players and fans
item.description: At the U.S. Open, artificial intelligence is giving players and fans a new way to experience the tournament.
